Cooling appearance and reheating disappearance differ; an operational image/turbidity threshold is not independently established equilibrium criticality or a universal minimum molecule count.

No new direct molecular force, solvent structure, dielectric or calorimetric measurement is admitted.

No exact common composition or ratio is silently selected. The qualitative recovery trace is admitted, with no new precise diffusion coefficient.

FRAP recovery depends on bleach geometry, imaging, diffusion/exchange assumptions and the fluorescent tracer. It supports mobility in the reported droplet preparation, not all constituent dynamics, DNA transport kinetics, viscosity, universal liquid character or proof that every condensate/coacervate has the same mechanism.

Background-subtracted emission per region volume is a concentration/partition proxy; equal quantum yield/dye behavior across phases and free-energy calibration are not independently verified.

boundary.value: Thermal, FRAP and DNA partition are three separate source preparations. This disordered terminal-region system is not a folded-helicase catalytic assay or a universal coacervate model.

changedFactor.value: Cooling/reheating in the thermal sample; local photobleaching in FRAP; ssDNA/dsDNA probe selection and inside/outside sampling in separate partition samples.

conditions.value: Thermal: 202 micromolar protein, 200 mM NaCl, pH 8, 50→22 C and reheat at 4 C/min. FRAP: 20 C, nominal 150 mM NaCl; main/SI mixture conflict. Partition: nominal 162.5 micromolar total protein, 150 mM NaCl, 1 micromolar DNA; source K=outside/inside.

controls.value: Repeated thermal cycles on the same sample; no-DNA fluorescence background; ten inside/ten outside regions in each of three fields in partition assay.

interpretation.value: Reversible source-specific demixing, tracer mobility and fluorescent-solute redistribution are supported. These observables do not establish a catalytic or metabolic advantage.

observable.value: Droplet/turbidity appearance/disappearance, qualitative fluorescence recovery, and background-subtracted confocal DNA-associated signal.

participants.value: Supplied Ddx4N1 residues 1–236; separate fluorescent Ddx4YFP/CFP tracers; separate labeled 32-base ssDNA/32-bp dsDNA preparations.

resources.value: Supplied purified protein, fluorescent tracers/DNA, buffers and imposed temperature cycles.

response.value: Cooling forms dense droplets and reheating disperses them with hysteresis. Separate FRAP shows qualitative recovery. Separate partition images enrich ssDNA-associated and deplete dsDNA-associated signal inside droplets.

timeScale.value: Thermal Figure 3D uses 4 C/min, distinct from 2 C/min cloud-point sampling. FRAP droplet is roughly 10 micrometers. Exact new recovery time/diffusion constant and catalytic observation window are not admitted.

uncertainty.value: FRAP mixture and DNA dye annotations conflict; no exact new diffusion, partition/free-energy or intrinsic affinity inferred. Functional consequence is unmeasured, not zero.

FRAP mixture and DNA dye annotations unresolved

studies.finding: The source reports RNA-product base-composition changes with different supplied DNA preparations and complementary composition for the selected single-stranded DNA input. This supports a finite DNA-dependent compositional constraint on RNA synthesis, without direct sequence fidelity, unique strand choice or complete in-vivo transcription regulation.
limitations: Distinct DNA preparations and synthetic copolymers are supplied to the enzyme fraction; composition assays have their own incubations and analytical methods. They are not identical to the standard CMP omission assay or one common biological template.
Bulk nucleotide composition agreement/complementarity does not determine nucleotide order, per-base mismatch frequency, promoter recognition or an end-to-end sequence-to-transcript mapping.

For the selected single-stranded phiX174 DNA comparison the RNA composition is close to the complement expected from the supplied DNA. This uses isolated bacteriophage DNA, not infection or a demonstrated replicating viral system.

For double-stranded DNA, average composition cannot uniquely identify strand selection. The source considers both strands serving, either together or separately, and explicitly notes uncertainty about transfer of isolated-DNA behavior to living cells.

The source discusses a more decisive direct DNA/RNA sequence comparison rather than performing that complete comparison here. Previously cited sequence work, later RNA-polymerase structures and modern transcription regulation remain outside this reading.
DNA-dependent ATP-only polyadenylate formation and the unresolved relation of the responsible activity to RNA polymerase constrain any universal faithful-transcript inference.

studies.finding: The source supports an enzyme-associated DNA-cage population, with proxy/calibration limits rather than universal exact pair occupancy.
limitations: This is a synthetic DNA-origami scaffold carrying commercially supplied enzymes, not a naturally evolved protein-only multienzyme complex, living metabolic network, protein biosynthesis or a cellular-origin experiment. The scaffold DNA is supplied; its sequence-dependent assembly was not independently reconstructed.

Negatively stained TEM, dye colocalization and photobleaching report different preparations/proxies. They support source-defined loading and location, not exact atom-level interfaces, universal pair occupancy, an impermeable shell or a measured protein-protein channel.

Photobleaching copy-number estimates normalize detected Cy3 steps to labels per free enzyme and depend on labeling, detection and six-state HMM assumptions. TableS3 covers HRP, G6pDH and beta-Gal, not direct proof that every cascade cage has exactly one GOx and one HRP.

Bulk cage concentration uses A260 and an adopted extinction coefficient0.109 nM^-1cm^-1; conjugate concentrations/labeling use absorbance deconvolution and inherited coefficients. Calibration, gel-extraction losses, active-enzyme fractions and labeling are not independently reproduced.

GOx/HRP activity is a coupled ABTS absorbance readout. It depends on both enzyme steps, intermediate availability, substrate concentrations and active fractions; it is not an isolated turnover count, direct intermediate trajectory, flux control coefficient or exclusive measure of substrate transfer.

The source nominally matches enzyme/cage concentrations but paired, separately caged and uncaged preparations differ in assembly, conjugation, purification, local environment and total cage/DNA organization. No isolated geometric confinement variable or equal active-site population is proven.

Separate full cages and half-cages also increase the coupled signal. Increased activity of a co-caged pair therefore does not uniquely establish direct substrate channeling, reduced intermediate escape or a proximity-only mechanism.

Hydration-layer ordering, electrostatic stabilization and conformational-substate mechanisms are proposed interpretations. Salt/helix-density comparisons alter more than one property and do not directly measure local water structure, local pH or a unique mechanism.

The single-molecule G6pDH enzymology uses a different enzyme, surface immobilization, PMS/resazurin reporter and 10 percent PEG. It is not the same GOx/HRP bulk cascade preparation or an independent replication of its fold enhancement.

The main/SI trypsin protocol annotations differ in digestion buffer, pH, enzyme concentration and assay ABTS concentration. No new protection/aggregation or persistence claim is admitted from those conflicting annotations.

No crosstalk suppression, competing-pathway insulation, local concentration gradient, intermediate residence/retention, synchronized feedback, closed metabolic cycle, sustained living-system regulation or universal efficiency benefit is measured in the admitted contexts.

The full main article and selected SI passages were read; most individual-enzyme kinetic traces and exact staple-sequence tables were not. Source ratios are approximate reported normalizations, not a new fit, digitization, data replay or independently reconstructed uncertainty.

Complete base TBS salt composition and an exact common active-enzyme population are not supplied/reconstructed; source concentration/normalization conventions are retained.
